title: COMPLETE-from-a-dep does NOT release that dep's pending DIRTY contribution (wedges a multi-dep node): a dep that emits DIRTY then COMPLETE WITHOUT an intervening DATA/RESOLVED leaves _depDirty[idx]=true and _pending>0 — the INVALIDATE arm clears this (EC3) but the COMPLETE/ERROR arms do not. A multi-dep node (e.g. deps [D,E], D dirties then completes, E live) then has _pending stuck >0 → _maybeRun/_tryRun is gated forever → the node never recomputes or settles. NOT hit by the normal inner lifecycle (sources emit DATA-then-COMPLETE, or bare COMPLETE with no prior DIRTY), so the *Map first cut is unaffected.

title: @graphrefly/ts resumeAll spurious undirty RESOLVED while paused: a buffered tier-3 emit does NOT set _emittedSettleThisWave (it is set only in the post-buffer down loop, node.ts ~line 900), so a COMPUTE node recomputing while paused under pausable:'resumeAll' has its DATA buffered yet still hits the _runWave undirty synthesis (wasDirty && !_emittedSettleThisWave) → emits a spurious RESOLVED via _emitToSubs that BYPASSES the pause buffer and reaches subscribers mid-pause
trigger: a consumer uses pausable:'resumeAll' on a COMPUTE node (deps>0) whose fn recomputes while paused. LOW-IMPACT + untested: resumeAll is B9-partial with NO conformance scenario. Surfaced by the graphrefly-rs CSP-6 Slice A /dev-dispatch (2026-05-30): the Rust arm sets emitted_tier3 when a tier-3 is BUFFERED (recognizing the settle at buffer time = the more-correct reading of R-resolved-undirty), avoiding the spurious RESOLVED; the TS arm lags. FIX: in TS node.ts _down, set _emittedSettleThisWave when a tier-3/4 msg is deferred into the pause buffer (mirror the Rust per-language choice). Pairs with B9 (resumeAll fidelity). PARITY NOTE: Rust resumeAll is currently MORE correct than TS on this axis — a deliberate per-language divergence (D24), not a spec change.

title: graphrefly-rs DeferredCtx holds a STRONG Core (Rc<RefCell<NodeInner>>): an async fn that stashes ctx.defer() and never emits (abandoned/cancelled work, a never-resolving backend) pins the node's NodeInner — and thus its fn slot (blocking the B32 unregister), its captured upstream Cores, and its dep_unsubs subscriptions — alive until the DeferredCtx drops. In correct usage the DeferredCtx drops when the async work completes/aborts (no leak), and the strong hold MATCHES TS's GC-reachability (the async callback closure keeps the TS node alive until it resolves). But it makes the dispatcher invoke's stale-handle no-op comment unreachable for this path (a strong Core can't have dropped+recycled), and a switchMap-style cancel that drops the DeferredCtx late over-retains until then
trigger: the real async-pool runner lands (B1) — decide strong-vs-Weak hold for DeferredCtx. Weak<RefCell<NodeInner>> (upgrade at emit, drop silently if gone — matching the dep-sink discipline) makes Drop/B32 reachable + the stale-handle no-op real, but silently drops an async result if the Node handle was dropped first (arguably wrong for an async source you want the result from). Surfaced by the CSP-6 Slice A /qa (2026-05-30, Blind Hunter). Low urgency: no leak in correct usage, no conformance path; revisit with the async runner.

title: describe() transitive auto-discovery of unregistered live deps (D51 follow-up): the D51 first cut auto-discovers ONE level — a registered node's DIRECT live deps that aren't in _entries (a *Map inner). An inner that ITSELF carries a subtree of unregistered nodes (e.g. project returns a composed node, not a leaf source) shows the inner but NOT its sub-deps. Reframe describe as a call-time LIVE-REACHABILITY walk (seed = registered nodes, follow live _deps, emit every reached node incl. transitively-unregistered ones) so deeper inner topology falls out for free.
trigger: a USER wants clearer / deeper live topology — i.e. a real consumer composes *Map inners that are non-leaf (carry their own unregistered sub-graph) and needs describe to show below the first inner level. Until then one-level is enough (most inners are leaf sources of/fromPromise). Per-language inspection (D24), no conformance; needs a per-graph WeakMap<Node,syntheticId> for stable unregistered ids.

title: R-terminal-settles-dirty x PAUSE/batch cross-axis (CSP-2.7 /qa 2026-05-30): the absorbed-terminal undirty RESOLVED (node.ts _settleAfterAbsorbedTerminal) emits via bare _emitToSubs. The gap is ONLY resumeAll-pause (must buffer the tier-3 settle slice, R-pause-modes) + open-batch (must defer to commit, D12) — a PARTIAL LATENT VIOLATION of those already-locked rules, not a fresh open question. The fix = route BOTH undirty RESOLVEDs through _down, which PRESERVES default-mode immediacy (_shouldBufferOnPause returns false for a default-mode sync emit) while buffering resumeAll + deferring batch. (The sawData->_maybeRun recompute already coalesces correctly under pause via _pausedDepWaveOccurred; only the RESOLVED balance bypasses.) Non-paused/non-batch is correct + conformance-covered (C-15 a-d, mutation-verified). THEORETICAL — no consumer, no failing test — parallel to B24 (rewireNext x batch/pause), deferred; contrast D44/D50 which were locked on a CONCRETE /qa symptom (garbage value / spurious ERROR), which this lacks. User chose DEFER 2026-05-30.
trigger: a consumer terminates/INVALIDATEs a dirtied dep while the receiving node is in resumeAll-pause or an open batch() AND needs precise settle timing (default-pause is already fine per D50); OR a deliberate cross-axis cleanup pass. THEN /spec-amend (the terminal analogue of D50): pin the undirty-RESOLVED settle timing — default immediate / resumeAll buffer / batch defer (= route through _down) — in R-resolved-undirty (or a focused new rule) + a conformance variant (C-16: terminal-mid-dirty under resumeAll + under batch) + formal coverage; fix BOTH receive-arms together for consistency (terminal _settleAfterAbsorbedTerminal AND the pre-existing INVALIDATE arm); then the Rust dep-terminal slice (B35) builds it in first time. title: completeWhenDepsComplete x an absorbed (errorWhenDepsError:false) errored dep never auto-completes: all_deps_complete requires EVERY dep_terminal==Some(Complete), so a dep that ERRORed (recorded Some(Error)) blocks the auto-COMPLETE cascade forever, even after all OTHER deps complete. A rescue/catch operator (errorWhenDepsError:false + completeWhenDepsComplete:true) over a stream whose one source errors-then-others-complete never emits its terminal COMPLETE. Parity-consistent: TS _allDepsComplete is identical (tm!==true -> false for an errored dep). Surfaced by the CSP-6 Rust /qa (Blind Hunter, finding 4).
trigger: a real rescue/catch operator (errorWhenDepsError:false) needs a terminal-but-errored dep to count toward completion (i.e. all deps TERMINAL rather than all deps Complete). Resolve via /design-review (does an absorbed-error dep count as settled-terminal for completeWhenDepsComplete?) -> pin in R-deps-terminal + a conformance scenario; fix BOTH arms together. NOT hit by any current scenario (no Rust/TS rescue operator wires this); deep in rescue-operator territory.

title: PROTOCOL-PULL design question (Fork B blocker, deferred to a NEW /design-review session): should GraphReFly add a protocol-level PULL -- a DEMAND/REQUEST tier (the callbag type-1-up analogue) so a sink can REQUEST data UP the conveyor belt and the source responds with DATA DOWN on demand, creating a DECLARED, inspectable pull-edge? USER'S LOAD-BEARING FRAMING (reframes the naive view): a PROTOCOL pull HONORS the guard -- a declared DEMAND edge appears in describe (D3/L0.7 inspectable topology satisfied); whereas the EXISTING method-pull (node.cache / lineage get()) is the actual BYPASS -- an invisible side-channel read outside the protocol. So 'pull breaks inspectability' is TRUE ONLY for method-pull (.cache); a declared protocol-pull is inspectable. LINEAGE: raw callbag HAS talkback pull (sink sends type-1-up no-payload = 'give me' -> source sends type-1-down = value; same type-1 both directions); callbag-recharge (the foundation GraphReFly is built on) ALREADY dropped it -- REFLOW-SPEC §1.4 up = PAUSE/RESUME/INVALIDATE/TEARDOWN (control only), chose METHOD-pull node.get() (cached read, MAY recompute-when-disconnected) over message-pull because of F-SYNC-CORE (message-pull is an async-style request/response round-trip, awkward in a sync wave core; get() is synchronous recursive DAG eval, glitch-free by construction); clean-slate inherited this (.cache = renamed get(), node.ts:200; R-data-not-peek scopes .cache to EXTERNAL consumers, bans in-graph .cache-peek to keep topology inspectable).
trigger: NEXT CHAT SESSION (user-scheduled): a fresh /decision-guard -> /design-review -> (if approved) /spec-amend to assess 'how much trouble vs how much benefit' of protocol-pull. BLOCKERS to amend: D9 (closed 9-tier set has NO DEMAND/REQUEST tier -- 'adding a tier is a constitutional change') + D8/R-ctx-up (up = control-tier only). DESIGN CHALLENGES to assess: (1) DAG pull-coordination -- a sink D pulling through a diamond (B,C over A): request fan-out, response fan-in, compute-A-once memoization; (2) F-SYNC-CORE reconciliation -- a synchronous request/response round-trip in the sync wave core (the reason the lineage chose method-pull); (3) interaction with two-phase push + ROM/RAM caching + lazy activation (does protocol-pull COMPLEMENT push or REPLACE part of it?); (4) tier/wave semantics (is DEMAND its own tier? how does it coexist with DIRTY/DATA?). BENEFITS to weigh: inspectable on-demand pull (vs the invisible .cache bypass), restored callbag pull/push duality, lazy eval through the protocol, a cleaner reactiveCollection (delta-stream push + snapshot pull ALL through the belt -- no external .cache side-channel). GATES Fork B (CSP-2.8 data-structures emit/delivery shape): whether reactiveCollection's snapshot is delivered via lazy-push items (no protocol change) OR a protocol-pull determines the emit design. Until resolved, Fork B (D55) is NOT locked; CSP-2.8 data-structures is ~90% designed (Fork A=D54 locked, shared scan-accumulator core + mechanical dissolutions set, composition=D56, storage=D57, render mechanical) with ONLY the snapshot-delivery/emit shape pending on this.
